items.title: Opposition in uproar over Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri's photos with Jeffrey Epstein
items.summary: Opposition leaders in India are demanding explanations after photos of Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri with convicted sex offender Jeffery Epstein began circulating on social media earlier this week. Leader of Opposition (LoP) Rahul Gandhi alleged that the photos had been released a day after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s India visit as “blackmail”. “Rubio goes to Mumbai. The US DOJ releases a picture of Epstein and Puri. Dear BJP and RSS workers, which anti-national traitor do you think they're blackmailing?” Rahul said on October 21. However, the photos are from dataset 9 released by the US Department of Justice (DOJ) in January. At least 10 photos taken at various angles show Epstein and Puri seated at a table, seemingly alone, deep in conversation with each other. The photos appear to contradict Puri’s claim in February that he had only met Epstein as part of a delegation. In a statement to The Wire, Puri’s office claimed that the minister could not recall, almost ten years later, which meeting the photograph showed or whether others were present before or after it was taken. items.title: Surety hurdles, questions over video, then release: The SEM proceedings for CJP leaders
items.summary: After hours of proceedings, repeated scrutiny of sureties and a police request for further custody, Cockroach Janata Party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka stepped out of Tihar jail on Wednesday night, after a release order by the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court at Mandir Marg police station. The duo had been in custody since October 13 after they allegedly jumped over a barricade and waved the Tricolour in the Jantar Mantar area. Two FIRs were subsequently filed, at least one of which has been transferred to the Delhi Police Crime Branch. They had been in custody for allegedly violating their peace bond – custody that was extended by two days on October 19. Newslaundry spent the day tracking the proceedings in the SEM court and the Delhi High Court, where they withdrew their plea challenging the judicial custody after being told they had an alternative remedy available.
